theme: HUMANSECS plate age labels + ISOAGE SLA gate

tests.name: old_deny
tests.cmd: Y2K age human weeks; gate deny REQUIRE2

weaknesses.title: HUMANSECS↔PARSEMS unit family mismatch (secs label vs ms value)
weaknesses.detail: HUMANSECS 90 → '1m30s'; PARSEMS LAST → 90000 (ms). Agents comparing PARSEMS result to ISOAGE seconds get 1000× error unless MS2SEC. No PARSESECS dual.

weaknesses.title: Huge ages produce week-heavy labels (ops noise)
weaknesses.detail: Y2K age → 1387w6d… No HUMANSECS_MAXUNIT or day-cap for digests.

weaknesses.title: No dual that formats seconds and returns seconds in LAST_N
weaknesses.detail: HUMANSECS sets HUMANSECS_N=input secs but LAST is string; PARSEMS of LAST is ms. Easy shuttle confusion with HUMANMS (ms in/out).

weaknesses.title: Zero-arg HUMANSECS uses prior LAST_N — silent if LAST is string path
weaknesses.detail: Chain after path-producing ops needs explicit secs arg.

workarounds: Always MS2SEC after PARSEMS of HUMANSECS labels before comparing to age_s
Store max/age as integer seconds on plate, not only human labels
Prefer HUMANSECS for second clocks; HUMANMS only for ms budgets
language_gaps: PARSESECS dual of HUMANSECS (label → seconds not ms)
HUMANSECS max unit / compact mode for multi-week ages
Documented unit family matrix (ms vs s clocks)
issues_faced: ms-vs-secs PARSEMS pitfall is core lesson for HUMANSECS agents
selftest green; no language fix this iter
